channel.description: Latest articles from The Meridian Star (meridianstar.com)

item.title: Restoring Mississippi’s ballot initiative in 2026: Long road, real stakes, narrow chances
item.description: For the fifth straight year, lawmakers went back to the Capitol promising to “give the people their voice back.” That voice is the ballot initiative—Mississippi’s century-old experiment with direct democracy—and the 2026 session may be the best shot in years to restore it.

item.title: Bogeys and Stogies golf tournament to benefit Illuminations Center for Dyslexia
item.description: Golfers and non-golfers alike are invited to take a swing for a good cause as the Bogeys and Stogies Golf Tournament takes place Friday, March 20, at Lakeview Golf Course.

item.title: Extreme cold watch issued as freezing temps return
item.description: Lauderdale County residents will want to bundle up heading into the weekend as another round of bitter cold moves through the area. An extreme cold watch has been issued for much of the state from Friday night through 6 p.m. Saturday.

item.title: Great Southern Bank donates $86,000 to Hope Village
item.description: Great Southern Bank announced this week a donation of more than $86,000 to Hope Village for Children in partnership with the Mississippi Charitable Tax Credit Fund. The tax fund allows businesses to make contributions to qualifying organizations and receive a tax credit.

item.title: East Mississippi Community College set to open 2026 baseball season
item.description: East Mississippi Community College’s 2026 baseball season is set to get underway Thursday Jan. 29 with an 11 a.m. doubleheader at Marion Military Institute in Marion, Alabama.

item.title: Hunting the wind
item.description: For a hunter, I don’t know if there’s a feeling any worse than that of getting winded by a deer.

item.title: Rep. Guest says appropriations, cost of living highest priorities
item.description: Mississippi Congressman Michael Guest said passing annual appropriations bills and focusing on cost of living issues for Mississippi residents will be his priorities in the immediate future as another funding fight looms on the horizon in Washington.

item.title: Our View: Domestic violence registry is unfortunately needed
item.description: State Senators and Representatives from all areas of Mississippi are in Jackson as the 2026 Legislative Session continues. The yearly meeting of elected officials sees thousands of bills introduced to change laws or policies, but the vast majority of them never make it past the first hurdle.

item.title: Supervisors discuss striping for county roads, Long Creek Reservoir dam
item.description: Several more roads in Lauderdale County are up to receive striping and reflectors as county supervisors are expected to vote Monday to award a striping package.
